journeys.title: Buying a seat

moments.say: Alice puts seat s1 on hold.
Bob wants the same seat and is turned away.
A moment passes while she pays.
Alice confirms; the seat is hers.

journeys.goal: Alice wants seat s1 and needs a moment to pay.

journeys.title: A hold that runs out

moments.say: Alice puts seat s1 on hold.
More time passes; the hold has run out.
Alice tries to confirm, too late.

journeys.goal: Alice puts a seat on hold and then does nothing.

journeys.title: Changing one's mind

moments.say: Alice puts seat s2 on hold.
She cancels the sold seat, and it is free again.

journeys.goal: Alice buys a seat and later gives it back.

examples.text: Hold a seat, then confirm it
A hold runs out after two time units and another customer can take the seat
One tick is not enough for a hold to run out
A third hold by the same customer is refused
An expired hold cannot be confirmed
The holder can cancel a sold seat, which frees it
Another customer cannot confirm someone else's hold
A seat the customer already holds cannot be held again
Confirming frees a hold slot: after a seat is sold the customer may hold two more

code.setup:
from app.reservation import ReservationService
class Clock:
    now = 0
    def tick(self):
        self.now += 1
clock = Clock()
system = ReservationService(['s1', 's2', 's3'], lambda: clock.now)

assumptions: Three seats and two customers (alice, bob) stand for any number; three seats are needed to show the limit of two holds.
A hold lasts 2 units of time here; the search stops at time 3, so later holds are never seen to expire.
Payment is outside the model: confirming a held seat always succeeds.
